### What does this PR do?

Proposes explicit validation of the k1/k3 estimator/update-mode combinations discussed in #8423. A detached k3 reward does not give the reverse-KL policy gradient, even at an exactly on-policy update with no clipping; it can ascend that KL. The loss kernels and PPO implementation are unchanged.

This is a **breaking configuration proposal**, pending maintainer agreement on the intended semantics of k3+PG:

- Reject k3/low_var_kl with `use_policy_gradient=True`; direct reverse-KL PG users to k1/kl.
- Change the Python dataclass PG default to False, matching the existing YAML default and retaining k3 as the default estimator.
- Extend the existing rejection of direct-backpropagation k1 to its equivalent kl alias.
- Document migration and add CPU construction/conversion and exact expected-gradient tests.

If k3+PG intentionally defines another reward-shaping objective, please clarify that intent before adopting this restriction. Direct supervised k3 remains available and is not claimed to be an equivalent reverse-KL PG update. Related to #8423; separate from #8386's numerical-cancellation fix.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched existing open PRs: [issue reference](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8423+in%3Abody), [estimator/update mode](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22use_policy_gradient%22+%22low_var_kl%22). No duplicate open PR found on 2026-10-30. The independent verification in the Issue does not link a published implementation; the report author is coordinating the contribution.
- [x] Title: `[BREAKING][algo, cfg] fix: validate distillation estimator update modes`.

### Test

New tests: `python -m pytest tests/workers/config/test_distillation_config_on_cpu.py -q`.

The complete 25-case test file against an isolated unmodified checkout gives **7 failed / 18 passed**, exactly the missing validation and default mismatch. The proposed code passes all new tests. The focused suite below gives **64 passed, 1 deselected, 7 existing warnings**:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/workers/config/test_distillation_config_on_cpu.py tests/test_base_config_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_config_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_actor_config_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_rollout_config_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py -k 'not test_command_with_override' -q --tb=short
```

Local Windows validation used the existing uv-created Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13 CPU environment with additional audit dependencies appended to the process module path. The excluded existing CLI test launches an unavailable Windows `python3` alias. Warnings come from existing test collection, Hydra and TP configuration. Changed-file `ruff`, `ruff-format`, `mypy`, and `git diff --check` pass. Full-repository hooks, Linux/GPU CI and model training were not run.

Gradient tests call the real `distillation_loss` API and enumerate all actions with fixed sampling weights. They compare the exact expected estimator gradient against true reverse-KL autograd and central finite differences, check inactive clipping, and verify a stationary equal-distribution case and KL-reducing SGD steps for unequal mild, severe, swapped and three-action distributions. There is no model download or running teacher worker.

**Baselines:** The failing baseline comparison and human test rerun used `2ab35292039a51175a4b3d3b3b2d76e951a0d3e4`. Before publication, Git connectivity was restored and the patch was rebased onto latest main `321e4e450fcfc47a3491c946cd01dacd9ea7281a`; `git range-diff` confirms the reviewed patch is unchanged. Codex reran the focused suite on that latest baseline: **64 passed, 1 deselected, 7 warnings in 6.36s**. Remote CI has not yet been run.

### API and Usage Example

```python
DistillationLossConfig()  # k3, direct supervised loss; matches existing YAML
DistillationLossConfig(loss_mode="k1", use_policy_gradient=True)  # reverse-KL PG
DistillationLossConfig(loss_mode="kl", use_policy_gradient=True)  # equivalent alias
DistillationLossConfig(loss_mode="k3", use_policy_gradient=True)  # now ValueError
```

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md.
- [x] Document compatibility changes and add CPU tests collected by the existing `*_on_cpu.py` workflow glob.
- [ ] Full-repository pre-commit checks; only changed-file Ruff/format/mypy were run locally.
- [x] Human submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line and understanding the complete change, and personally ran the local verification script: **64 passed, 1 deselected, 7 warnings in 5.25s** on 2026-10-30.
- [ ] Request project CI through the documented channel when ready; no request has been sent.

AI assistance: Codex prepared the patch and ran the CPU checks. The mathematical report and pre-existing local alias tests informed this proposal. The independent commenter's unpublished candidate was not used. The human submitter confirmed line-by-line review and understanding and provided the successful personal test rerun output before submission. No model-quality improvement is claimed.

Why don't we reject other non-negative losses, like k2?

> using a detached k3 reward omits a parameter-dependent term.

Not clear what this means. 

I also think the explanation can be made more intuitive: 

k3 is non-negative, so it does not encode whether the student assigns too much or too little probability to a token. When used as a negative reward in REINFORCE, the update favors actions with lower k3 relative to other actions, which need not correspond to moving toward the teacher.

+from verl.trainer.distillation.losses import distillation_loss

+    settings = {"loss_mode": loss_mode, "use_policy_gradient": False}

+            DistillationLossConfig(**settings)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("loss_mode", ["k3", "low_var_kl"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("from_omegaconf", [False, True])
+def test_k3_aliases_reject_policy_gradient(loss_mode, from_omegaconf):
+    """Reject detached k3 rewards through direct and OmegaConf construction."""
+    settings = {"loss_mode": loss_mode, "use_policy_gradient": True}
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="reverse-KL policy gradient"):
+        if from_omegaconf:
+            omega_conf_to_dataclass(OmegaConf.create(settings), dataclass_type=DistillationLossConfig)
+        else:
+            DistillationLossConfig(**settings)
+
+

+    """Keep Python construction compatible with the existing YAML defaults."""

+        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "verl/trainer/config/distillation/distillation.yaml"
+    )
+    config = DistillationLossConfig()
+    assert config.loss_mode == yaml_config.distillation_loss.loss_mode == "k3"
+    assert config.use_policy_gradient is yaml_config.distillation_loss.use_policy_gradient is False

+)

+    """The guard must preserve PG k1 aliases and supervised k3 aliases."""

+    assert config.loss_settings.use_estimator
+    assert not config.loss_settings.use_topk
+

+        ([0.6, 0.4], [0.55, 0.45]),
+        ([0.99, 0.01], [0.01, 0.99]),
+        ([0.8, 0.2], [0.2, 0.8]),
+        ([0.2, 0.8], [0.8, 0.2]),
+        ([0.2, 0.3, 0.5], [0.5, 0.4, 0.1]),
+    ],
+    ids=["equal", "mild", "severe", "opposing", "swapped", "three-actions"],
+)

+    """The exact expected API gradient must match autograd and finite differences of reverse KL."""
+    student_probs = torch.tensor(student_probabilities, dtype=torch.float64)
+    teacher_probs = torch.tensor(teacher_probabilities, dtype=torch.float64)

+    log_probs = logits.log_softmax(dim=-1)
+    teacher_log_probs = teacher_probs.log()
+    reference_kl = (log_probs.exp() * (log_probs - teacher_log_probs)).sum()
+    reference_gradient = torch.autograd.grad(reference_kl, logits, retain_graph=True)[0]
+
+    finite_difference = torch.empty_like(logits)

+        delta = torch.zeros_like(logits)
+        delta[index] = 1e-6
+        plus = (logits.detach() + delta).log_softmax(dim=-1)
+        minus = (logits.detach() - delta).log_softmax(dim=-1)
+        plus_kl = (plus.exp() * (plus - teacher_log_probs)).sum()
+        minus_kl = (minus.exp() * (minus - teacher_log_probs)).sum()
+        finite_difference[index] = (plus_kl - minus_kl) / 2e-6

+        n_gpus_per_node=1,
+        nnodes=1,
+        teacher_models={

+            use_policy_gradient=True,
+            use_task_rewards=False,
+            loss_max_clamp=None,
+            log_prob_min_clamp=None,
+        ),
+    )

+        ratio = (sampled_log_prob - sampled_log_prob.detach()).exp()
+        assert 1.0 - config.distillation_loss.clip_ratio_low < ratio.item()
+        assert ratio.item() < 1.0 + config.distillation_loss.clip_ratio_high
+        data = TensorDict(

+                "prompts": torch.tensor([[0]]),
+                "responses": torch.tensor([[action]]),
+                "attention_mask": torch.ones(1, 2, dtype=torch.int64),
+                "response_mask": torch.ones(1, 1, dtype=torch.bool),
+                "old_log_probs": sampled_log_prob.detach().reshape(1, 1),
+                "teacher_logprobs": torch.stack([teacher_log_probs[action], teacher_log_probs.new_zeros(())]).reshape(
+                    2, 1
+                ),
+            },
+            batch_size=[],
+        )
+        tu.assign_non_tensor(data, dp_size=1, batch_num_tokens=1, global_batch_size=1)
+        output = {"log_probs": torch.stack([sampled_log_prob, sampled_log_prob.new_zeros(())])}
+        loss, _ = distillation_loss(actor, config, output, data)
+        # Sampling weights are fixed when taking the expectation of the SGD estimator.
+        expected_loss = expected_loss + student_probs[action].detach() * loss
+
+    actual_gradient = torch.autograd.grad(expected_loss, logits)[0]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_gradient, reference_gradient, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12)
+    updated_log_probs = (logits.detach() - 0.01 * actual_gradient).log_softmax(dim=-1)
+    updated_kl = (updated_log_probs.exp() * (updated_log_probs - teacher_log_probs)).sum()

+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_gradient, torch.zeros_like(actual_gradient), atol=1e-12, rtol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(updated_kl, reference_kl.detach(), atol=1e-12, rtol=0)
+    else:
+        assert updated_kl < reference_kl.detach()

inline_comments.body:
> using a detached k3 reward omits a parameter-dependent term.

Not clear what this means. 

I also think the explanation can be made more intuitive: 

k3 is non-negative, so it does not encode whether the student assigns too much or too little probability to a token. When used as a negative reward in REINFORCE, the update favors actions with lower k3 relative to other actions, which need not correspond to moving toward the teacher.

+            use_policy_gradient=True,
+            use_task_rewards=False,
+            loss_max_clamp=None,
+            log_prob_min_clamp=None,
+        ),
+    )
+    # Validated configuration only; no model, worker, distributed group, or GPU is created.
+    expected_loss = logits.sum() * 0.0
+    for action in range(student_probs.numel()):
+        sampled_log_prob = log_probs[action]
+        ratio = (sampled_log_prob - sampled_log_prob.detach()).exp()
+        assert 1.0 - config.distillation_loss.clip_ratio_low < ratio.item()
+        assert ratio.item() < 1.0 + config.distillation_loss.clip_ratio_high
+        data = TensorDict(
+            {
+                "prompts": torch.tensor([[0]]),
+                "responses": torch.tensor([[action]]),
+                "attention_mask": torch.ones(1, 2, dtype=torch.int64),
+                "response_mask": torch.ones(1, 1, dtype=torch.bool),
+                "old_log_probs": sampled_log_prob.detach().reshape(1, 1),
+                "teacher_logprobs": torch.stack([teacher_log_probs[action], teacher_log_probs.new_zeros(())]).reshape(
+                    2, 1
+                ),
+            },
+            batch_size=[],
+        )
+        tu.assign_non_tensor(data, dp_size=1, batch_num_tokens=1, global_batch_size=1)
+        output = {"log_probs": torch.stack([sampled_log_prob, sampled_log_prob.new_zeros(())])}
+        loss, _ = distillation_loss(actor, config, output, data)
+        # Sampling weights are fixed when taking the expectation of the SGD estimator.
+        expected_loss = expected_loss + student_probs[action].detach() * loss
